{
  "edges": [
    {
      "fromKey": "n-ufqg50",
      "toKey": "n-1lq9li6",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The work was paused (event) because the pressure dropped at P-R while upstream remained normal. The area directory does not establish valve positions or pressures, so it cannot explain why the drop occurred; rather, its limitation is a condition that prevents using it to determine cause.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1","b678a928-a8d2-472d-bc03-2e1a3dc411e6#1"],
      "claimIds": ["finding-jkn4le", "claim-ojcuoi"],"counterfactual":"If the area directory had established valve positions, it might have revealed a closed or mispositioned downstream valve as the cause of localized pressure loss.",
      "competingExplanation": "The drop could be due to upstream supply fluctuation not captured by sampled data (n-1sd8vsk), but evidence shows P-U remained stable at ~6.9 bar, making this unlikely.","evidenceGap":"Need continuous or more frequent sampling of the distribution path between North gallery and RHOB receiving header H-R to rule out transient upstream events missed by sparse samples."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-ufqg50",
      "toKey": "n-16kxawb",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The work was paused because the air-low indication occurred. No line opening was authorized at that time, meaning no formal isolation procedure had been completed to protect against this hazard.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds":["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1","eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds": ["finding-h3ez7i", "claim-ojcuoi"],"counterfactual":"If a line opening had been authorized before the interruption, work could have continued safely or isolation would have prevented exposure to low-pressure conditions.",
      "competingExplanation": "The lack of authorization may stem from incomplete boundary preparation rather than an oversight; however, evidence shows maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed (n-85pdam), supporting this interpretation.","evidenceGap":"Need documentation showing whether the crew attempted to obtain line-opening authorization before the interruption or why it was deferred until after restoration."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-oigq1p",
      "toKey": "n-2jmrrk",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The temporary instruction attachment field was blank at issue time, indicating incomplete documentation of any service-routing changes or hazard controls. This contributed to the lack of formal authorization for work continuation.",
      "status": "unknown",
      "sourceIds":["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds":[],"counterfactual":"If the temporary instruction attachment had been completed, it might have documented necessary hazard controls or service-routing changes that would explain how work proceeded safely despite low pressure.",
      "competingExplanation": "The blank field may simply reflect administrative delay rather than a failure to document; however, given the criticality of instrument-air systems during maintenance preparation, even minor documentation gaps can be hazardous.","evidenceGap":"Need evidence showing whether any verbal or informal communication occurred between Utilities and RHOB regarding service-routing changes that might explain why no formal attachment was needed."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1sd8vsk",
      "toKey": "n-1lq9li6",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The pressure extract provides only sampled values and excludes data from all locations or valve states, limiting the ability to determine whether the drop was localized or systemic. This limitation prevents using it as definitive evidence of cause.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds":["fcd254db-75b3-4a9d-abec-44c5b6a9b34e#1","da0260c0-7d49-43e8-b074-da2a14c7d59c#1"],
      "claimIds":["finding-jkn4le", "claim-ojcuoi"],"counterfactual":"If continuous monitoring had been available, it might have captured transient events or valve states that explain the localized pressure drop.",
      "competingExplanation": "The sampled data may still be sufficient if combined with other evidence such as shift logs and point registers; however, without more granular data, causal links remain uncertain.","evidenceGap":"Need access to continuous monitoring records for instrument-air distribution paths or additional sampling points between North gallery and RHOB receiving header H-R."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-17qciec",
      "toKey": "n-2jmrrk",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The shift log records 'boundary preparation in progress' but does not identify the point of interruption or valve states, contributing to uncertainty about whether proper isolation procedures were followed.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds":["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1","eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds":["finding-jkn4le", "claim-ojcuoi"],"counterfactual":"If the shift log had identified the point of interruption or valve states, it might have revealed whether proper isolation procedures were followed before work began.",
      "competingExplanation": "The lack of detail may reflect standard logging practices rather than an oversight; however, given the criticality of instrument-air systems during maintenance preparation, even minor documentation gaps can be hazardous.","evidenceGap":"Need evidence showing whether any verbal or informal communication occurred between Utilities and RHOB regarding service-routing changes that might explain why no formal attachment was needed."
    }
  ],
  "decision": {
    "summary": "The investigation identifies multiple contributing factors to the instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation. Key findings include: (1) localized pressure drop at P-R while upstream remained stable, suggesting a downstream issue; (2) incomplete documentation of service-routing changes or hazard controls due to blank temporary instruction attachment field; (3) lack of formal line-opening authorization before work continuation; and (4) limitations in monitoring data that prevent definitive determination of cause. Evidence gaps include need for continuous monitoring records, clarification on whether verbal communications occurred regarding service-routing changes, and documentation showing why no formal attachment was needed.",
    "evidenceUsed": ["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1", "eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1", "b678a928-a8d2-472d-bc03-2e1a3dc411e6#1", "fcd254db-75b3-4a9d-abec-44c5b6a9b34e#1"],
    "unknowns": ["Whether any verbal or informal communication occurred between Utilities and RHOB regarding service-routing changes that might explain why no formal attachment was needed.", "Need for continuous monitoring records to capture transient events missed by sparse samples."],
    "alternatives": [
      "The pressure drop could be due to upstream supply fluctuation not captured by sampled data (n-1sd8vsk), but evidence shows P-U remained stable at ~6.9 bar, making this unlikely.",
      "The lack of authorization may stem from incomplete boundary preparation rather than an oversight; however, given the criticality of instrument-air systems during maintenance preparation, even minor documentation gaps can be hazardous."
    ],
    "confidence": 0.75
  },"evidenceRequests":[

]
}
